newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends off lows, lead zooms to $700.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends off lows, lead zooms to $700.

text.p: Copper prices managed a moderate bounce on Thursday afternoon after initially coming off a high of $2,175, while tight nearby spreads remained the market's primary focus.
The other LME metals largely range-tradeed, excluding lead which trundled up above the $700 level to clinch a strong close.
Three-months copper finished the kerb at $2,148 a tonne, down $15 from Wednesday after failing to hold above the $2,150 level.
Nearby spreads remained tight and were the focus for the day ahead of "third Wednesday" pricing. Cash for a day was last bid at $21 backwardation, while cash for two days was around $40.
In the first ring heavy volume had been done in tomorrow/next day which mainly traded at a $22.50 backwardation, close to the LME's limit of one percent of the cash price.
Cash to threes narrowed, however, which reflects tight dates dropping out of the frame ahead of the December date coming into play. The spread was last at $127, down from $140 on Wednesday.
Traders said the strong backwardations had been attracting metal into LME warehouses and they expected stocks to rise on Friday between 5,000 and 10,000 tonnes.
Overall volumes were reasonable despite relatively quiet ring sessions in copper, traders said.
Lead pushed higher on buying throughout the day, in part by delta hedging against call options on the back of earlier Far Eastern buying, traders said.
When speculative buying pushed it through the $690 level, stops were triggered sending lead to a high of $703 in the ring. It finished at $700, up $21 and the highest since November 27.
"Some people were waiting for stop-loss selling to appear, and when it didn't, lead got a bullish close," a trader said.
Aluminium finished just $1 higher than on Wednesday at $1,528, close to the centre of the day's range. It followed copper off its lows of $1,513.
Nickel similarly finished virtually changed at $6,705, despite an early crumble to a low around $6,660. But weak technicals left it vulnerable to a drop to November 18 low of $6,600, analysts said.
Zinc finished $9 stronger at $1,058, tin was $40 higher at $5,830, while alloy was last bid $5 firmer at $1,367.
